newsitem.title: UK: NWE fuel barges softer, 1 pct cargoes talked highe.
newsitem.headline: NWE fuel barges softer, 1 pct cargoes talked highe.

text.p: The European high sulphur fuel oil barge market eased on Tuesday with traders saying two players were trying to push prices in different directions.
High sulphur cargoes were quiet in an unchanged market while low sulphur cargoes were talked slightly stronger.
High sulphur barges were bought a few times by a European major at $86 fob Rotterdam but were later sold by a trading house between $85.50 and $84 a tonne.
The major was said to be bidding the higher price as it had a contract for bunkers while the trading house was reported keen to drive prices down as it was eyeing a Russian M-100 cargo loading today.
No trades were reported in the high sulphur cargo market.
One seller was reported to have delayed the loading of a cargo it was recently offering at $81 fob until July while a trading house was still offering its cracked material at $79 fob.
One percent was talked a little higher with one major said to be offering a cargo at $95 fob, 25 cents a tonne higher than last bought on Friday by a trading house.
Supply and demand were seen as balanced.

"Supply and demand are fairly steady, one buyer scared the market last week and bought a whole bunch of stuff but now a couple of people are offering. It is a fairly quiet market," a trader with a major said.

A trading house confirmed that the 75,000-tonne cargo it picked up on Friday was coupled with a 40,000 tonner bought from a French refiner at a floating price that day and the lot would be heading out of the area.
Traders said the possible homes for the combined cargo were Israel, Italy or Cuba.
